world_parts_with_shadow — SEGMENTATION world op

• Data kinds: none → table (an op determined by its arguments alone — it takes no image or data input)

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.world_parts_with_shadow(seed: 'int' = 0, *, size=(200, 260), n_parts: 'int' = 3, light_angle: 'float' = 35.0, shadow_length: 'float' = 9.0, noise: 'float' = 0.02) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import segworld; segworld.world_parts_with_shadow(seed: 'int' = 0, *, size=(200, 260), n_parts: 'int' = 3, light_angle: 'float' = 35.0, shadow_length: 'float' = 9.0, noise: 'float' = 0.02) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opssegmentation.get("world_parts_with_shadow"))

Usage

World of industrial parts (rotated rectangles with circular holes) with oblique-lighting shadows, facet shading and highlights (world_parts_with_shadow).

Light is parallel light shining in the direction light_angle (degrees, from the image x axis towards the y axis). Shadow = the part mask shifted by shadow_length in the light direction, minus the parts themselves (holes let the light through). The side of a part's face that faces the light is bright, the far side about as dark as the shadow (the reason a threshold is fooled). Highlights are Gaussians near the edge on the side facing the light.

Returns: image, labels (parts 1..n), shadow (bool), truth = {n_parts, parts (center, w, h, angle, holes), areas (w h − Σ π r²), shadow_offset (dy, dx), shadow_area (measured pixel count), light_angle}.
